1.explanation:
1. We define an array of objects, each containing an icon component and some metadata.  
2. We pass those objects to Dropdown as the items prop.  
3. We implement itemToElement so the menu shows our icons instead of text.  
4. We deliberately implement itemToString to return the raw object, which Downshift will coerce to a string via toString(), resulting in “\"[object Object]\"” in the button’s title attribute.  
5. When you open the menu and select an icon, the dropdown button shows the icon visually, but hovering it reveals the title tooltip “ [object Object] ”—this reproduces the bug described.
1.bug_scenario: In this scenario we’re using Carbon’s Dropdown component to render a list of icons by hijacking the itemToElement callback. Each dropdown option is an object with an icon component on it, and we intentionally return the full object from itemToString so Downshift will string-coerce it. Visually the list items show our custom icons correctly, but when you select one the button’s title attribute (and thus its tooltip) becomes "[object Object]" instead of something meaningful or the icon itself.
